rationale: Unattested verb in the corpus. Tentatively from ⲱⲗⲉ 'afflict, distress' with Lycopolitan prosthetic ⲟ-vowel. In context (line 14: 'the holy man habitually ⲟⲁⲗⲟ his body in the fast in order to grasp the entire archontic in him'), the verb names the ascetic discipline of the body in fasting. Alternative readings 'release/depart' (from ⲟⲩⲱⲗ) or 'purify' cannot be ruled out. Confidence low pending parallel attestations.

Verbal stem appearing in ⲉⲩϣⲁⲛⲟⲱ 'when they perform' (line 28). Possibly from ⲟⲩⲱ 'complete, have already done' used as a full lexical verb of performing/fulfilling the four works of fasting. Tentative.

Form in line 3 ϩⲙⲟⲩⲛ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'established forth.' Possibly Lycopolitan reflex of ϣⲙⲟⲩⲛ 'establish' or related to ⲱϩⲉ ⲙⲟⲩⲛ 'stand abiding.' The cosmogonic context (separations of Light/Darkness, beautiful/bad established by primal divine action) supports the establishment-sense. Confidence low.

Greek loanword σύγκρασις 'mingling, mixture.' Standard Manichaean technical term for the cosmogonic mingling of Light and Darkness. Used here in the body-microcosm: the soul entering through nourishment carries the mingling of darkness which the fast cleanses out.

Lyc. ⲛ̄- (genitive) + ϩ- prosthetic + ⲡⲱⲣϫ̄ 'separate, divide' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲱⲣⲭ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'separate forth'). Substantival use 'the separation' here names the Manichaean primal cosmic act distinguishing Light from Darkness.

Verb in line 22 ⲛ̄ⲥⲉϣⲱⲟⲉ ⲁⲣⲁⲥ 'they are not injured by her.' Tentatively from ϣⲱⲱϥ 'be defiled, harmed' or related stem. The sons of the Light suffer no destruction from the nourishment — they remain pure. Confidence low; flagged for parallels.
